chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said:

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله prayed with his companions during the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ. He divided his companions into two groups: he stationed one group facing the enemy and another group behind him. Then he pronounced the takbīr and they pronounced the takbīr; he recited and they listened silently; he performed rukuʿ and they performed rukuʿ; he performed sajdah and they performed sajdah. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله remained standing, and they prayed one rakʿah for themselves. Then some of them gave salām to others, then they went out to their companions and stood facing the enemy. Their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and he pronounced the takbīr, so they pronounced the takbīr; he recited and they listened silently; he performed rukuʿ, so they performed rukuʿ; he performed sajdah, so they performed sajdah. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sat and recited the tashahhud, then gave salām to them. They then stood and completed one rakʿah for themselves, then some of them gave salām to others.

key_terms.بِإِزَاءِ العَدُوِّ: positioned facing the enemy in a defensive stance
key_terms.رَكَعَ: he performed rukuʿ, the bowing part of salat
key_terms.رَكْعَةً: a unit of prayer completed by each group
key_terms.غَزَاةِ ذَاتِ الرِّقَاعِ: the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ, the setting of this event
key_terms.فَأَنْصَتُوا: they listened silently during the recitation
key_terms.فَتَشَهَّدَ: he recited the tashahhud while seated
key_terms.فَسَجَدَ: he performed sajdah, the prostration in salat

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله perform the Prayer of Fear during battle?
ai.summary: This hadith describes how the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله performed salat al-khawf during the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ by dividing the companions into two groups. It shows a practical form of prayer in conditions of danger, combining worship with vigilance against the enemy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1334 - Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"The Prophet (sw) prayed with his companions during the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa'. He divided his companions into two groups: one group faced the enemy, while the other stood behind him (for prayer). He commenced the prayer with them by saying the takbir, and they all said the takbir. He recited, and they listened silently. He bowed, and they bowed. He prostrated, and they prostrated.
Then the Messenger of Allah (sw) remained standing while they prayed an additional rak'ah for themselves and then exchanged positions. The first group took their place facing the enemy, and the other group came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah (sw). He then repeated the takbir, and they followed. He recited, and they listened silently. He bowed, and they bowed. He prostrated, and they prostrated.
Then the Messenger of Allah (sw) sat for the tashahhud and offered the salutation (ending the prayer). Afterward, this group completed another rak'ah for themselves, and then they exchanged greetings with one another."
